status: EXECUTED — 2026-08-04. Every case below runs as a real test against mobile/shared/protocol/ (the single Kotlin implementation, ADR-007) via :shared:testDebugUnitTest. Green on JVM. NOT executed on Kotlin/Native yet — see runner_gaps.

count_correction_2026_08_04.headline: case_total was 99. It is 110. NO VECTOR WAS ADDED, REMOVED, OR CHANGED — the manifest was simply counting inconsistently, and running the vectors for the first time exposed it.
count_correction_2026_08_04.what_was_wrong: Per-file counts used different rules per file. key_schedule.json declared 11 (its `cases` array only, silently excluding 5 `property_assertions` and 3 `invalid`). display_jitter.json declared 8 (excluding 4 `property_assertions`). key_rotation.json declared 34, which matched no rule at all — the file holds 18 `cases` + 2 skew windows + 6 self-eid cases + 6 `invalid` + 1 `accepted_not_rejected` = 33.
count_correction_2026_08_04.why_it_mattered: A manifest that misstates its own contents launders unexecuted cases into a green count. 'All 99 pass' was unverifiable by construction, because no consistent reading of these files yields 99.
count_correction_2026_08_04.the_rule_now: A CASE is one named, independently executable assertion unit: every entry of `cases`, `invalid`, `property_assertions`, `skew_window_across_seam`, `self_eid_rejection.cases`, `accepted_not_rejected`. Pinned by VectorManifestTest, which recomputes the counts from the files on every CI run and fails on drift. It cannot silently rot again.
count_correction_2026_08_04.consumer_action: 40-contracts BLE wire v0.1 says 'conformance vectors: ... 99 cases'. That line needs an orchestrator edit to 110. No behaviour changed; no platform needs to re-run anything it had already passed.

unaffected_by_ADR_008.headline: ADR-008 made account_key server-issued. ZERO existing vectors were regenerated. Not one hex value moved.
unaffected_by_ADR_008.why: A conformance vector tests the function (account_key, day, epoch) -> ephemeral_id. ADR-008 changed WHO PRODUCES the input to that function, not the function. HKDF does not know or care about the provenance of its IKM. The salt is unchanged, both info strings are unchanged, both output lengths are unchanged, the epoch and day arithmetic is unchanged, and the frame layout is unchanged.
unaffected_by_ADR_008.regenerating_them_would_have_been_harmfu: The property that makes a vector file useful is that a diff in it means a diff in behaviour. Rewriting 65 files to record a prose change would have destroyed exactly that property, and the next reviewer would have had to diff 65 files to discover that nothing changed.
unaffected_by_ADR_008.revalidated_anyway: All 11 key_schedule.json cases were re-derived on 2026-08-04 against a SECOND independent implementation (Node crypto.hkdfSync) as well as the original OpenSSL 3.5.6 generation. Both agree. This was cheap paranoia, not a change.
files_added: key_rotation.json — genuinely new normative rules (key ring, seam, self-eid rejection) that did not exist before ADR-008

description: Conformance vectors for the Radius BLE wire protocol. The single Kotlin implementation in mobile/shared/protocol/ must pass all of these. Both platforms consume that one implementation (ADR-007), and CI runs these vectors as the regression net.
how_to_use: Each file is table-drivable: read `cases`, feed the inputs, assert the expectations.
Hex strings are lowercase and contain no separators. An empty string means zero bytes.
Floating-point expectations carry a `tolerance` object at file level. Discrete values (bands, error codes) must match exactly.
A failing vector is a build failure, not a warning.

files.kind: rejection, one error code per case, deterministic ordering
full AD assembly and parsing, both carriers, hostile inputs
HKDF-SHA256 known-answer + rotation property assertions + fault cases
account_key ring resolution, rotation seam, skew window across a seam, self-eid rejection, superseded-key destruction, malformed rings
stepwise Kalman + normalisation + hysteresis sequences. 9 cases, 76 asserted steps.
HMAC-SHA256 known-answer for displayed metres + anti-averaging properties

case_total_note: Recounted 2026-08-04 under one consistent rule (see count_correction_2026_08_04): that recount produced 110 with NO vector added, removed or edited. 116 is 110 plus the 6 genuinely new `destruction_at_seam` cases in key_rotation.json, added the same day to cover KEY_SCHEDULE.md §8.5.2, which was normative and unimplemented until then. Under the old inconsistent count the pre-existing set had been reported as 99.
counting_rule: One case = one named, independently executable assertion unit. Sections counted: cases, invalid, property_assertions, skew_window_across_seam, self_eid_rejection.cases, destruction_at_seam, accepted_not_rejected.

provenance.key_schedule.json: HKDF-SHA256 via OpenSSL 3.5.6, first verified against RFC 5869 test case 1. Not hand-written.
provenance.key_rotation.json: Ephemeral IDs are either reused verbatim from key_schedule.json or generated the same way (OpenSSL 3.5.6, HKDF-SHA256). The ring-selection expectations were then re-derived end-to-end by an independent reference implementation (Node crypto.hkdfSync) and all agree. Not hand-written. The `destruction_at_seam` cases (2026-08-04) introduce NO new hex: every eid in them is one of the values already asserted elsewhere in the same file, queried a second time after a prune. That is deliberate — the new property is 'this value is no longer derivable', and it is only meaningful if the value is one we have independently proven WAS derivable.
provenance.banding.json: Generated by a reference implementation of BANDING.md executed over the input sequences. Not hand-written.
provenance.frame_valid.json / frame_invalid.json /: Constructed by hand from the byte layout in SPEC.md §3 and §5, cross-checked for length.

runner.implementation_under_test: mobile/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/radius/shared/protocol/ — the single Kotlin implementation both platforms consume (ADR-007).
runner.reads_the_real_files: The runner loads these JSON files FROM DISK through this manifest. It does not use an embedded or generated copy, because a copy can drift and a drifting copy destroys the only property that makes a vector file worth keeping: that a diff in it means a diff in BEHAVIOUR.
runner_gaps: KOTLIN/NATIVE IS NOT COVERED. commonTest has no filesystem, so the runner lives in the JVM test source set. It therefore proves the SHARED implementation's arithmetic, but not that the Kotlin/Native backend produces identical results for it. Closing this needs a build-time codegen step that embeds the vector text into a generated commonTest source — a change to mobile/shared/build.gradle.kts, which is android-kotlin's file. HANDOFF raised.
There is no Mac (B4), so no iOS target compiles at all today. The gap above is scheduled, not urgent.

not_covered_here: Anything requiring a radio. These vectors test arithmetic and parsing only.
Discovery latency, battery, band accuracy versus true distance, RPA co-rotation.

Those require real hardware and an external BLE sniffer. A green vector run says the codec is correct; it says NOTHING about whether the protocol works on air. Do not report a vector pass as spike validation.

error_codes_added_v0_1.E_NO_ACTIVE_KEY: no key ring entry is effective at the queried (day, epoch). A gap is a fault, never a silent empty result. KEY_SCHEDULE.md §8.2
error_codes_added_v0_1.E_KEY_RING_NOT_MONOTONIC: two entries share an effective boundary, or kid order disagrees with effective_from order. Either means two keys could be active at once, which is the exact state the seam rule forbids. KEY_SCHEDULE.md §8.2
error_codes_added_v0_1.E_SELF_EID: an observed frame carries one of the receiver's OWN ephemeral_ids within its own accepted window. Drop before resolution. KEY_SCHEDULE.md §9.6
